//: Hymmnos for content strings that live in src/content/ rather than in the
interface catalog. English stays the single source of truth there, so only
the layer text is stored here and the two are matched by key rather than by
copying the English twice.
Summary keys are named for the record. Body keys carry a hash of the
paragraph text as the browser renders it, not as it is written: the markdown
processor rewrites apostrophes and dashes, so a key hashed from the source
would never match. Editing a paragraph retires its key and the layer falls
back to English rather than showing a translation of the old wording.
src/lib/prose-key.mjs derives the keys and the client resolves them.
Licence identifiers are the one thing held back inside a translated licence
paragraph. MIT and GPL-3.0 name a specific document with specific terms, and
a reader who needs to know which one applies must be able to read it in any
layer; the sentence around it carries no such weight and is translated.
Product names, file formats, and languages stay in English for the same
reason: they are names, not words. Translating osu!mania or USC would
describe nothing and would break the one thing a reader can still search
for. tests/language-layer.test.mjs masks them by the same list it uses for
the interface catalog, so anything outside that list must still be attested
vocabulary.
